body.p: Thanks for having me on the show
Happy to. So you bake bread for a living
I do, mostly sourdough
and a few sweet things on weekends
How early does your day start
Around four in the morning
The ovens need an hour to heat up
and the dough has been resting overnight
What's the first thing you check
The smell, honestly
If the starter smells sharp
I know it's ready to go
And if it doesn't
Then I feed it and wait
There's no way to rush it
Do you ever get tired of waiting
Not really, it's the quiet part of the day
I make coffee and sweep the floor
What goes wrong most often
Too much water in the mix
The loaf spreads out flat
and the crust never gets crisp
How do you fix that
You don't, you start again
and you measure more carefully next time
Is there a loaf you're proud of
A dark rye with caraway seeds
It took me two years to get right
What changed in the end
A longer bake at a lower heat
and a tray of water under the rack
Do customers notice the difference
Some do, and they tell me
Most just come back the next week
What would you tell a beginner
Buy a cheap scale and use it
Write down what you did each time
and don't worry about the shape
Any plans for the shop
Maybe a second oven next spring
and a small table by the window
That sounds lovely
Thanks again for coming in
Thanks for having me on the show
